title: Beyond Orbital Rotations: Correlation-Rank Limits and Clifford-Accessible Measurement, from Algebra and Global Optimization
summary: One should not assume that reconstructing an electronic observable with a smaller set of measurement settings will cut the number of repetitions in proportion. Each setting is simply a basis change and qubit readout, but the savings are not guaranteed to be commensurate. Take two electrons of opposite spin in two spatial orbitals: the orbital degree of freedom of each electron acts as a logical qubit and rotations are independent in the spin sectors. From the observable's one- and two-qubit coefficients we derive an exact floor for the setting count and a decomposition to meet it in no more…
